messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 1793141592 - 03:42 UTC - error-rate spike detected for hosted inference (us-west1). 5xx rate from model-pool-3 jumped from 0.2% -> 12% over 2 minutes. Auto-retries increasing. Paging maya (oncall-engineering).

maya: On it. joining bridge. seeing 502/504 on /v1/generate. Can someone grab logs and tail the dispatcher? :eyes:

chris: I have console open. Looks like a sudden increase in timeouts from grpc-worker-2 to model shard. Latency at 2.3s and then 504. No config changes in last 24h.

ashwin: I'm pulling recent kernel and oom logs, but memory usage on the node pool is normal. Could be a degraded network path or a bad model rollout. Checking model rollout dashboard now.

maya: @sre-lead can you confirm if autoscaling kicked in? Also start an immediate mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from us-west1 if possible 2) fallback to smaller model variant for high QPS routes 3) update status page draft.

sre-lead: Autoscaling hasn't increased capacity yet; policy is conservative due to latency SLOs. I'll bump target capacity for the pool and enable burst for 10m. Executing:
```bash
# bump pool target to +3 instances
redwood infra scale --pool model-pool-3 --delta 3 --reason "emergency scale"
```

chris: Doing canary rollback of most recent model variant (v2026-03-10-rc2) to previous stable (v2026-02-28). If this is a model regression, that should stop the timeouts.

ashwin: Network checks look OK from infra side. I see increased connection errors between grpc-worker-2 and storage backend; retry logic might be amplifying. I'll temporarily increase retry backoff and reduce parallelism on affected workers.

maya: Support please draft customer-facing note for immediate status page and a targeted email for customers who had requests served by us-west1 in the last 2h. Include clear, concise impact and next steps. Keep it high-level, avoid speculation on root cause until security/legal weigh in.

support-lead: Drafting now. Suggest two artifacts: 1) status page entry 2) targeted customer email. Drafts below — please review, edit.

support-lead: STATUS PAGE (initial):
"2026-06-23 03:42 UTC — Degraded performance in US‑West hosted inference. Some requests may return errors (5xx) or experience increased latency. Engineers are investigating and routing traffic to healthy regions where possible. We will provide updates within 30 minutes."

support-lead: CUSTOMER EMAIL (targeted):
"Hi — We detected degraded performance for some inference requests served from our US‑West region between 03:40–04:00 UTC on 2026‑06‑23. During this window, a subset of requests may have returned errors or experienced higher latency. Our engineering team is routing traffic to healthy regions and rolling back a recently deployed model variant as a mitigation. We will follow up with a full incident summary once root cause is confirmed. If you saw an operational impact, reply to this message and we will prioritize your case."

legal: Hold on the customer wording with the sentence about rolling back a model variant — avoid implying code-level regressions without confirmation. Also, we need to review whether this rises to a required disclosure under privacy/security rules if any request logs were potentially exposed or retried to incorrect endpoints. @security please advise on scope.

security: Quick note — we have no evidence yet of unauthorized access. The TTL for request logs in the region is 30 days; we need to confirm whether any redirected retries could have crossed tenant boundaries (unlikely but must be verified). I'll start a limited audit: check access logs for cross-tenant headers and any 200 responses to unexpected endpoints. ETA 40m.

maya: Understood. For now redact the customer email line about the rollback. Keep the status page minimal and factual. Support, update drafts: remove model rollback mention.

support-lead: Updated CUSTOMER EMAIL (v2):
"Hi — We detected degraded performance for some inference requests served from our US‑West region between 03:40–04:00 UTC on 2026‑06‑23. During this window, a subset of requests may have returned errors or experienced higher latency. Our engineers are routing traffic to healthy regions and working on mitigation. We will provide a follow-up incident report once root cause is confirmed. If you experienced an outage, please reply and include request IDs (if available)."

sre-lead: Scaling completed, burst enabled. Pool CPU/memory stable. Rolling traffic away from us-west1 via routing policy to us-central1 and eu-west1 for stateless endpoints.

chris: Rollback completed on canary traffic. Observing error rate drop to 1.1% and latency back to normal on the canary set. Will continue to monitor before wide rollbacks.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://calls.redwood.com/bridge/1793141592 - participants: maya, chris, ashwin, sre-lead, support-lead, security, legal.

maya: Quick mitigation checklist I'm using — please weigh in: 
- Isolate affected pool (model-pool-3) : done
- Enable emergency burst: done
- Route traffic to healthy regions: in progress
- Rollback risky model canary: in progress
- Customer/Status page notice: draft complete (support-lead)
- Security audit for cross-tenant exposure: security assigned
- Postmortem owner: TBD (engineering + SRE)

legal: If audit finds cross-tenant exposure or data leakage, we must notify customers within our SLA and follow regulatory timelines. Start preparing the customer disclosure template with the following required sections: 1) What happened (summary), 2) What data may have been affected (scope), 3) Mitigations taken, 4) Actions we will take, 5) Contact and reporting options. Keep items 2 and 5 conditional on audit results.

security: Noted. I also recommend we preserve all relevant logs and lock down retention for the affected buckets until the investigation closes. Send a DM to infra to snapshot logs.

ashwin: Taking snapshots of logs now. Executing:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/us-west1/ /tmp/us-west1-logs/ --recursive --profile incident --quiet
# snapshot to secure bucket
aws s3 sync /tmp/us-west1-logs/ s3://redwood-incidents-snapshots/1793141592/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```

support-lead: Internal incident comms template (for SEs/customer success to use):
"Short update: We are currently investigating degraded inference performance in US‑West. Engineers are mitigating and routing traffic; we do not have evidence of data exposure at this time. We will send another update within 30 minutes or when we have new info. If you'd like a call, reply and we'll schedule."

maya: Nice. Add a line: "If specific customers saw production errors, collect request IDs and tenant IDs and tag them on the status page internal field for follow-up."

support-lead: Added.

security: Audit preliminary: no cross-tenant 200 responses observed in first 4000 requests checked. A small number of retries resulted in duplicate processing but within the same tenant context. Continuing deeper check, ETA 25m for full traversal.

chris: Error rate across pool down to 0.9% after canary rollback + scaling. Marking mitigation as effective; continuing monitoring for 60m.

maya: OK — moving to observe stage. Handing off to night shift oncall at 04:15 UTC. @chris will be primary for next 60m, @ashwin take secondary, and @sre-lead will join on escalation. Please maintain incident notes and update status page if anything changes.

chris: Copy. I'll create the post-incident timeline skeleton and assign postmortem owner (likely SRE).

legal: We'll standby for the security audit outcome. If anything changes indicating exposure, I'll prepare the required disclosure letter.

security: Full audit done: no evidence of cross-tenant data exposure. There were retries but they resolved to the original tenant. Closing scope: no PII leakage detected. We'll include logs and checks in postmortem.

support-lead: Preparing the follow-up status update (planned):
"2026-06-23 04:40 UTC — Update: Mitigations applied (traffic routing and model rollback) have reduced error rates. No evidence of data exposure from initial audit. Full incident report and timeline will be shared within 72 hours."

maya: Great. For the postmortem include: timeline, root cause analysis (model vs infra vs network), impact quantification (requests affected, customer list), mitigation steps, and prevention plan (tighter rollout gating, improved autoscale rules).

sre-lead: Assigning postmortem owner: @chris. Target postmortem draft in 48 hours.

chris: Will do. Adding action items: 
- Adjust autoscale policy to allow faster emergency ramp (owner: sre-lead, due: 2026-07-07)
- Add pre-deploy health gating for model rollouts (owner: eng-runtime, due: 2026-06-30)
- Improve retry/backoff defaults to avoid amplification (owner: eng-runtime, due: 2026-06-29)

incident-bot: Incident 1793141592 transitioned to MONITORING by maya at 04:15 UTC.

maya: Thanks everyone. Logging this thread into incident tracker and closing pager for now. If anything regresses, re-open the bridge. :thumbsup:
